independent_computation.step_1_what_the_leaf_asserts: item_coverage[].reason is the sourced justification for how (or whether) an item's effect is priced into the focus utility outcome. Both candidate strings are checkable factual claims about Zhonya's Hourglass as cached.

step_2_test_the_new_value_clause_A.claim: 'Every declared family on this item is a defence.'
step_2_test_the_new_value_clause_A.test: Enumerate the families/behaviors the cache declares for item 3157 and check each for defensiveness.
step_2_test_the_new_value_clause_A.result: FALSE. Both decompositions declare a non-defensive family. (a) stat/stats includes stat.ability_power = 105.0 flat AP, which is a purely offensive stat; (b) a 'damage' family is declared outright in both files (damage.resistance-mitigation in item-atoms, damage.basic_attack in atoms/items.json). A universal quantifier over declared families is refuted by a single counterexample, and there are two.

step_3_test_the_new_value_clause_B.claim: 'the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD.'
step_3_test_the_new_value_clause_B.test_i_stat_line: 105 AP x Syndra Q ratio 0.70 = 73.5 additional raw magic damage per Dark Sphere (before resistances), i.e. the item measurably raises outgoing damage. With 100/(100+R) mitigation at R = 60 that is still 73.5 x 100/160 = 45.9 post-mitigation damage per Q. Non-zero => the item does change outgoing TDD.
step_3_test_the_new_value_clause_B.test_ii_the_active_itself: The cached branch text says stasis leaves the user 'unable to move, declare basic attacks, cast abilities, use summoner spells, or activate items', and the wiki atom calls stasis a 'Full disable'. A 2.5 s full self-disable sets the user's damage output to 0 for 2.5 s, so even the active alone changes outgoing TDD (downward). Symmetrically, when the stasis belongs to the focus target, the attacker's damage over the window is reduced by up to 2.5 s of denied output. Either way the mechanic is not TDD-neutral.

step_4_test_the_old_value.claim_A: 'Time Stop is priced only from the explicit bounded active-seconds scenario input'
step_4_test_the_old_value.check_A: Supported and required by the cache: the effect is a duration, not a rate — 2.5 s per activation ({{fd|2.5}} in the branch text, 'Enter Stasis for 2.5 seconds' in riotDescription, values [2.5] units [flat] on atom control.stasis). A duration-typed effect can only enter a fight model as an explicit, bounded number of active seconds; 2.5 s per cast is the bound the cache supplies. Nothing in data/ contradicts this.
step_4_test_the_old_value.check_B: Supported: Time Stop is an active ('unique': true, listed under active[], simpleDescription 'Activate to become invincible but unable to take actions'). Owning the item does not put the champion in stasis; that requires a cast, and the cast costs the caster 2.5 s of full self-disable. Assuming stasis from possession would both invent an uncast active and silently apply its downside. Nothing in data/ contradicts this.
step_4_test_the_old_value.result: Both clauses TRUE and sourced; the string also preserves the two facts the cache actually pins (bounded duration, activation-gated).

independent_computation.step_5_conclusion: The old string is a fully sourced, correct statement about the cached item. The new string is refuted twice by the same cache: the item declares non-defence families (105 AP, plus an explicit 'damage' family in both atom decompositions), and the represented mechanic — a 2.5 s full disable — does change outgoing damage rather than being confined to durability. The new value is not a rewording of the old one; it drops the sourced bounded-duration/activation-gated facts and replaces them with a claim the data contradicts.
